    <p>
      I am an aspiring marine data scientist interested in applying new machine learning approaches to large oceanographic datasets to address practical questions in ocean science and management. Having lived and worked at sea since joining the Navy at 18, I have found myself continually drawn toward oceanographic research. I am particularly interested in the role of phytoplankton and algal blooms in ocean carbon cycling and the environmental processes that drive harmful algal blooms and their management.
    </p>
    <p>
      Over the past decade, I have had the opportunity to work on both sides of marine research: conducting oceanographic research at sea as a Marine Science Technician aboard the R/V Atlantic Explorer, and working with marine environmental data through Running Tide, a carbon-sequestration startup, and the Ecosystem Modeling department at Bigelow Laboratory for Ocean Sciences as a student intern.
    </p>
    <p>
      This portfolio brings together a selection of oceanographic data analysis projects. It represents my interest in using computational tools to better understand ocean systems and ultimately apply that understanding to practical problems in marine science and management.
    </p>
